retained_original_metadata.title: Unitarity of the closed-chain B_N separation-of-variables transform for inhomogeneous SL(2,R) positive discrete-series spin chains with spins greater than one half
retained_original_metadata.author: Sergey E. Derkachov; Karol K. Kozlowski; Alexander N. Manashov
retained_original_metadata.source_title: Completeness of SoV Representation for SL(2,R) Spin Chains
retained_original_metadata.difficulty_reason: The proof establishes surjectivity of a generalized eigenfunction transform on a continuous multivariable spectral Hilbert space, beyond formal orthogonality. It uses coupled inductive transforms, exact Mellin-Barnes integrals, gamma-factor regularization, and proved distributional delta limits to exclude orthogonal complements. The difficult analytic step controls an inverse overlap transform whose unregularized kernel has insufficient decay.

proof_review.note: Read the B-transform norm proof of Theorem 3.1, the coupled induction in Section 4 with Lemmas 4.1-4.3, and the complete distributional calculations in Appendix A. The A-transform isometry is explicitly the repeated regularized norm calculation with its displayed kernel, and the main new surjectivity argument is fully expanded. Gustafson integral identities and previously computed layer-operator overlaps are identified established background. Select only the Section 4 B_N unitarity conclusion, not three analogous transform claims. Preserve the author displays; the regularizer inequalities on page 19 are written without modulus although g_L is complex, and their use in norm integrals is explicitly a modulus estimate.

retained_original_metadata.statement_scope: The unlabelled final Section 4 unitarity conclusion restricted to T_N^B: H_N^B=L2(R_plus) tensor symmetric L2(R^(N-1),mu_N-1^B) -> tensor product H_N of upper-half-plane holomorphic discrete-series spaces. N finite, spins s_k>1/2 and real inhomogeneities xi_k, with kernels and measures exactly as Sections 3.1 and 2 define. Completeness means surjective unitary transform, not merely the Theorem 3.1 isometric embedding.
